belongs_to: Construct 4 'Square with a Hole' (Observe that the circular hole is the same as the centre of the square; Hint: Think where the centre of the circle should be)
description: A square drawn with a thin black outline and, inside it, one circle (thin black outline, no fill) whose centre is exactly the centre of the square. The circle's diameter is a little more than half the side of the square (about 0.58 of the side), so there is an equal margin of white space on all four sides of the circle. No labels, no measurements, no shading.

belongs_to: Construct 5 'Square with more Holes'
description: One large square with thin black outline, divided by one vertical and one horizontal line through its centre into 4 equal squares in a 2 x 2 arrangement (2 rows, 2 columns). Each of the 4 small squares contains exactly one circle (thin outline, no fill), centred in that small square; circle diameter about 0.58 of the small square's side, so every circle has equal margin from its own square's four sides and all 4 circles are identical. No labels, no measurements, no shading.

belongs_to: Construct 6 'Square with Curves' (This is a square with 8 cm sidelengths; Hint: think where the tip of the compass can be placed to get all the 4 arcs to bulge uniformly from each of the sides) - printed beside a 'Try This' badge
description: A square (side 8 cm according to the text; the figure itself carries no length label) with a black outline. Inside it, four identical circular arcs, one along each side: each arc starts at one corner of the square and ends at the neighbouring corner, and bulges INTO the square (towards the centre). So the four arcs meet in pairs at the four corners and together enclose a four-cornered concave (star-like) region in the middle, with each arc lying inside the square and touching the square only at its two end corners. The middle of each arc is about one-fifth of the side (roughly 0.2 x side) away from the side it belongs to. All four arcs are the same size and the figure is symmetric. No labels, no shading.
unclear: Exact radius / centre of the arcs is not given in the book; the depth of about 0.2 x side was measured from the picture only.

belongs_to: 'Consider a rectangle PQRS. Join PR and QS. These two lines are called the diagonals of the rectangle' (also used for the next page: 'In the figure, the diagonal PR divides angle R into g and h ... angle P into c and d')
description: A rectangle PQRS, wider than tall (about 1.7 : 1). Corners: P top-left, Q top-right, R bottom-right, S bottom-left (letters printed outside the corners). Both diagonals PR (top-left to bottom-right) and QS (bottom-left to top-right) are drawn and cross at the centre. Each of the 8 angles formed at the four corners between a side and a diagonal is marked with a small arc and a lowercase letter: at P: c (the lower angle, between side PS and diagonal PR) and d (the upper angle, between side PQ and diagonal PR); at Q: e (left angle, between side QP and diagonal QS) and f (lower angle, between side QR and diagonal QS); at R: g (upper angle, between side RQ and diagonal RP) and h (left angle, between side RS and diagonal RP); at S: b (upper angle, between side SP and diagonal SQ) and a (right angle, between side SR and diagonal SQ). So 8 small arcs and 8 letters a, b, c, d, e, f, g, h in total. No lengths or degree values are printed.

belongs_to: 'How will you record your observations? First, identify the parameters that need to be tracked. They are the sides of the rectangle and the 8 angles formed by the two diagonals' - blank recording table
description: An empty recording table with 9 columns and 3 rows. Header row (orange background, white bold text), left to right: 'Sides', 'A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E', 'F', 'G', 'H'. Below the header there are 2 completely empty body rows (light peach background, thin white cell borders, 9 empty cells each, 18 empty cells in all). No numbers, units or other entries are printed. (The columns A to H stand for the 8 angles marked a to h on the PQRS figure of page 17; the 'Sides' column is for the side measurements.)
unclear: Column headings are printed as capital letters A-H while the angles in the PQRS figure are lowercase a-h; a student must match them by order.

belongs_to: Construct 1 'Construct a rectangle in which one of the diagonals divides the opposite angles into 60 and 30' - Solution, 'Let us start with a rough diagram'

Corners: A bottom-left, B bottom-right, C top-right, D top-left (letters printed outside the corners). The diagonal AC is drawn from bottom-left to top-right. At D there is a small right-angle square mark inside the corner (only at D; no right-angle marks at A, B or C). At A the diagonal splits the right angle into two arcs-marked angles: the upper one between AD and AC labelled '30 degrees' (written as 30 with a small raised circle), the lower one between AC and AB labelled '60 degrees'. No lengths are printed.

belongs_to: Construct 1 Solution, 'STEP 1: AB is drawn with an arbitrary length. What is the next point that can be located?'

RIGHT panel: the same horizontal segment AB (same length, A left, B right, labels below) with a vertical line drawn upward from B, perpendicular to AB and about 1.7 times as long as AB; a small right-angle square mark sits inside the corner at B (above AB, left of the vertical line). No other marks or measurements.

belongs_to: Construct 1 Solution, 'STEP 2' (point C located)

belongs_to: Construct 1 Solution, 'STEP 4, Method 1: Draw a line perpendicular to BC at C to get the point D'

belongs_to: Construct 1 Solution, 'STEP 4, Method 2: Using a compass, mark the point D such that AD = BC. Join CD to get the required rectangle'
description: Two panels side by side, each with a compass drawn (grey/pink-red illustration of a pair of compasses with a hinge screw and a pencil clamp). LEFT panel: horizontal AB (A left, B right), a vertical line up from A, a vertical line up from B, and the 60 degree ray from A (arc and label '60 degrees' at A) crossing B's vertical at C (C labelled) and continuing a little beyond C. The compass is open with its two legs touching C and B, i.e. opened to the length BC. No right-angle mark in this panel. RIGHT panel: same lines (A left, B right with a small right-angle square mark at B, vertical lines at A and B, 60 degree ray crossing B's vertical at C, '60 degrees' at A); the compass legs now rest on A (lower leg) and on the vertical through A (upper leg, pencil end), and a short arc is drawn across the vertical line through A at the point labelled D (D printed just left/above the arc's crossing), located at the same height as C, so AD = BC.
unclear: Which compass leg is the needle and which is the pencil is not clear in the small illustration; only the span (BC in the left panel, A to D in the right panel) is certain.

belongs_to: Construct 2 Solution, 'STEP 1: The base CD measuring length 5 cm can be easily constructed. Next?'

belongs_to: Construct 2 Solution, 'STEP 2: Draw a perpendicular to line DC at the point C. Let us call this line l'

belongs_to: Construct 2 Solution, 'STEP 3, Method 1: Construct a circle of radius 7 cm with point D as the centre. ... The point where the circle intersects the line l is the required point B'

belongs_to: Construct 'House': 'Recreate this figure. Note that all the lines forming the border of the house are of length 5 cm' (and Construct 1 on page 29: 'a bigger house in which all the sides are of length 7 cm')
description: The house figure, symmetric about a vertical axis. Roof: a triangle with apex A at the top and base corners B (left) and C (right); sides AB and AC are straight lines, each labelled '5 cm' (AB label at its upper-left, AC label at its upper-right). The base of the roof is NOT a straight line: it is a circular arc from B to C that sags downward (bulges away from A, about 0.17 of BC deep, centre A, radius 5 cm). Body: below B and C two vertical straight sides BD (left) and CE (right), each labelled '5 cm' (to the left of BD, to the right of CE), and a horizontal base DE at the bottom. Under DE a double-headed arrow spans from D to E with the label '5 cm' in its middle. Door: a small rectangle standing on the base DE, centred horizontally on DE, 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall: label '1 cm' above it, label '2 cm' written vertically (reading upwards) on its left side. Point labels: A (top), B and C (ends of the arc / tops of the sides), D and E (bottom corners). Body BDEC is a 5 cm x 5 cm square with the arc instead of its top side; triangle ABC would be equilateral (AB = AC = BC = 5 cm).

belongs_to: House Solution, 'STEP 1' (first the lines forming the border below B and C)
description: Lower part of the house only, open at the top (U-shape): left vertical segment B (top) to D (bottom) labelled '5 cm' on its left; right vertical segment C (top) to E (bottom) labelled '5 cm' on its right; horizontal base DE joining D and E, with a double-headed arrow underneath it labelled '5 cm'; the door rectangle standing on DE in the middle (label '1 cm' above it, label '2 cm' written vertically on its left). Labels B, C at the top ends and D, E at the bottom ends. No roof, no point A, no arc, no line joining B and C.

belongs_to: House Solution, 'STEP 2: Draw a curve that has all its points of 5 cm from the point B; the circle centred at B should be with 5 cm radius. Does this help in spotting the point A?'
description: The Step 1 U-shape (B-D left side labelled 5 cm, C-E right side labelled 5 cm, base DE with double arrow '5 cm', door 1 cm wide and 2 cm tall with labels '1 cm' and '2 cm') plus one full circle with centre B and radius 5 cm. The circle passes through C (touching the right side CE at C, its rightmost point) and through D (its lowest point; it just touches the base line at D), so its top is 5 cm above B and its left edge 5 cm left of B. It cuts across the door rectangle (entering near the door's bottom-left and leaving near its top-right corner). B is the centre but there is no mark on it other than the letter B and the top end of line BD. Labels: B, C, D, E, '5 cm' x3, '1 cm', '2 cm'. Point A is not marked.
unclear: Exact crossing points of the circle with the door rectangle read from the picture only.

belongs_to: House Solution, 'STEP 3, Method 1: Take a radius of 5 cm in the compass and with C as the centre, draw a circle. Are you able to spot the point A? ... See the point at which both the circles intersect'
description: The Step 1 U-shape (B-D left side '5 cm', C-E right side '5 cm', base DE with double arrow '5 cm', door 1 cm x 2 cm with labels '1 cm' and '2 cm') with TWO full circles of radius 5 cm: one centred at B (passes through C and touches the base at D) and one centred at C (passes through B and touches the base at E). Each circle goes through the other's centre. The two circles overlap in a lens-shaped region and cross each other at two points on the vertical axis midway between B and C: the upper crossing (above the line BC, about 4.3 cm above it - this is the required point A, not lettered in the picture) and a lower crossing near the base that falls inside the door rectangle (visible as an X inside the door). Labels: B, C, D, E, '5 cm' x3, '1 cm', '2 cm'; no A.

belongs_to: House Solution, 'Method 2: So the point A could have been obtained just by drawing arcs of radius 5 cm from points B and C' (text on page 27; figure at top of page 28, followed by 'Join A to B and A to C by straight lines')
description: The Step 1 U-shape (B-D left side '5 cm', C-E right side '5 cm', base DE with double arrow '5 cm', door with '1 cm' and '2 cm') plus, high above the middle of BC, a small X made by two short crossing arcs, with the letter A at the crossing. A drawn compass (grey/pink-red illustration with hinge screw) has one leg's tip on C and the other leg (pencil end) at A, i.e. opened to 5 cm. No full circles and no lines AB or AC yet.

belongs_to: House Solution, 'STEP 4: Take 5 cm radius in the compass and from A, draw the arc touching B and C as shown in the figure. The house is ready!'
description: The completed house, same as the figure on page 25 (roof triangle with apex A, straight sides AB and AC each labelled '5 cm'; arc from B to C sagging downward; sides BD and CE labelled '5 cm'; base DE with double arrow '5 cm'; door 1 cm x 2 cm with labels '1 cm' and '2 cm'; letters A, B, C, D, E) with a compass illustration (grey/pink-red) drawn at the top right: one leg on A and the other leg with the pencil end at C, showing the arc BC being drawn about centre A.

belongs_to: Hints A) Eyes (from 8.1 Artwork and Construct above): 'Part of the construction is shown earlier ... Points A and B are the locations where the tip of the compass is placed ... where should these points A and B be placed?' (Construct 2: recreate 'Eyes')
description: A partly constructed eye in dark red-brown lines. Centre: a lens-shaped eye (pointed at left and right) made by an upper arc and a lower arc; the lens is filled with pale blue-grey. A thin horizontal line runs through the middle of the lens and sticks out a little to the left of the left tip. The curve beyond the right tip runs down to the pencil end of a drawn compass whose other leg (needle) is at the dot labelled B, which lies far below and slightly to the left of the lens centre. A second dot labelled A lies far above the lens, vertically in line with B and the lens centre. To the right of the eye, separate from it, a second horizontal line of the same colour (about as long as the lens is wide) is drawn at the same height as the line through the eye. Labels: A (with dot, top), B (with dot, bottom); no lengths.
unclear: Exact positions of A, B and the arc centres are only approximate; the book asks the student to estimate them.

belongs_to: Hints B) (From Construct above, page 211): 'For the purpose of construction, let us take the side lengths to be of 5 cm. Consider this figure. We need to identify only one more point to make this a 4-sided figure. That point, D, should be 5 cm from both B and C'
